name: SMSR-2: High CPU Utilization Due to Anomalous/Malicious Activity
description: The on-board Health & Safety app reports the CPU-hogging indicator active — processor stress consistent with malicious code or a command flood. Read from the health telemetry partition.
query:
FROM logs.ecs.spacecraft.health
| WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hour AND fswApp == "HS" AND hs.cpuHogState == "ENABLED"
| KEEP @timestamp, fswApp, hs.cpuHogState, hs.statusFlags
| LIMIT 100
author: Elastic
false_positives: A scheduled compute-heavy payload task raises CPU legitimately. Tune the threshold and add exceptions per mission.
note:
## SPARTA Investigation Guide

### Detection logic
An ES|QL rule over the health telemetry that flags the HS app's CPU-hogging indicator active — processor stress from malicious code or a command flood.

### Framework reference
- **Tactic:** Execution
- **Technique EX-0010:** [Malicious Code](https://sparta.aerospace.org/technique/EX-0010/)
- **Indicator of Behavior SMSR-2:** Anomalously high CPU utilization from anomalous or malicious activity.

### Indicators of Behavior
- **SMSR-2: Anomalously high CPU utilization from anomalous or malicious activity.**

### How to validate this alert
Correlate with the command-flooding rule and any recent code/table load. Sustained high CPU on a spacecraft risks watchdog resets. See spartastixkb.
